sections.html:
Hammond is a city in Lake County, in the northwest corner of Indiana, on Lake Michigan and inside the Chicago metro area. It is the only Indiana city that borders Chicago.

The city runs from the lakeshore south to the Little Calumet River and from the Illinois state line west to east as far as Cline Avenue. It covers about 23.8 square miles, of which about 1.1 square miles is water. Lake George, Wolf Lake, Oxbow Lake and parts of the Grand Calumet River all sit inside or along its edge.

Much of the ground is former dune and swale on sandy soil that was leveled for development. The next section covers why water is a topic Hammond buyers raise.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Hammond's older houses?
sections.html:
Hammond was settled around 1847 by German immigrant farmers, and industry arrived in 1869 when the George H. Hammond Company opened a meatpacking plant. The city was named for that Detroit butcher.

It became a town on December 4, 1883, and the population climbed with the mills and rail yards until it peaked at 111,698 in 1960. The 2020 census counted 77,879 residents, which makes Hammond the eighth-largest city in Indiana.

That growth pattern left a large stock of early and mid-twentieth century housing: worker cottages, bungalows and two-flats. Several neighborhoods are listed as historic districts, including Forest-Ivanhoe, Forest-Moraine, Glendale Park, Indi-Illi Park, Pullman-Standard and Roselawn-Forest Heights. Houses of this age often need electrical, plumbing and foundation work, and the cost of that work is usually the biggest reason an owner considers a cash sale.

sections.h2: What are the main employers in Hammond?
sections.html:
Hammond's largest employers are a hospital, the school district, a casino and city government. The list below comes from the city's Wikipedia entry and shows approximate headcounts.

  • Franciscan Health Hammond: 2,500
  • School City of Hammond: 2,485
  • Horseshoe Casino: 1,866
  • City of Hammond: 875
  • Walmart: 785
  • Indiana Harbor Belt Railroad: 759
  • Lear Seating: 615

Manufacturers in town include Unilever, Atlas Tube, Cargill, Jupiter Aluminum and Dover Chemical, and ExxonMobil and Marathon Petroleum have oil storage here.

One change to know about: Franciscan St. Margaret Health, which had been the city's only hospital, closed in December 2022.

Yes, heavy rain has caused sewer backups and flooded basements in Hammond. On September 17, 2023, more than four inches of rain fell in seven hours, and a city press release reported sewer backups in more than 500 homes.

Mayor Tom McDermott Jr. urged homeowners to install backflow preventers, and the Hammond Sanitary District said it would reimburse residents up to $2,000 toward the installation, according to Lakeshore Public Media. Whether that program is still open is something to ask the Sanitary District directly.

If your Hammond house has had water in the basement, expect a buyer to ask about it. A financed buyer's inspector and lender will look at the damage, the repairs and the insurance history. A cash buyer will price the same issues, but without waiting on an appraisal or loan approval.

sections.h2: What does Hammond require of rental owners?
sections.html:
Hammond requires owners of rental housing to register every year, and the deadline is April 15. The rule is in the city code at section 96.152.

  • New rentals must be registered within 30 days of buying the property.
  • An owner who stops renting, sells or transfers a rental must notify the Inspections Department within 30 days.
  • The annual fee is $5 per unit, and the late fee is $500 per unit not registered by April 15.
  • Registration needs proof of insurance equal to the property's value, or a bond or letter of credit for the greater of the property's value or $25,000.
  • Fines for not registering can reach $2,500 per unit per day for a first violation and $7,500 for later ones.

If you own a Hammond rental and want to sell, report the sale to the city within the 30 days. Forms and the Code Enforcement office are at City Hall, 5925 Calumet Avenue, and the phone number is (219) 853-6300.

sections.h2: What permits and contractor rules apply in Hammond?
sections.html:
Hammond requires building permits for construction and remodeling, and every contractor working in the city must be registered with it. The Building Division is in Room G1 at City Hall, with Monday to Friday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and a phone number of 219-853-6317.

Plumbing work needs a state plumbing license, and the city lists a minimum plumbing permit fee of $50 that covers the first three fixtures. Heating and cooling contractors take a city exam, and electrical contractors are licensed through the Electrical Board.

If you plan to renovate before listing, ask the division what applies to your scope.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and recording work for a Hammond sale?
sections.html:
Lake County bills the property tax on a Hammond house, and the county treasurer collects it. The Lake County Treasurer has offices in Crown Point at 2293 N. Main Street, in Hammond at 232 Russell Street (219-933-2900) and in Gary.

The state's property tax page says Indiana has two installments a year, and the 2026 dates were May 11 and November 10. A payment up to 30 days late carries a 5 percent penalty, and after that the penalty rises to 10 percent.

Indiana also uses a sales disclosure form for conveyances. In the 2010 Justia copy of IC 6-1.1-5.5 that we read, the form goes to the county assessor and then to the county auditor before the deed is filed, and the recorder cannot record the deed without proof that the auditor received it. The process has been amended since, so your title company should confirm the current steps. Lake County's recorder is at the same Crown Point address as the treasurer.

sections.h2: How do transit and roads affect a Hammond sale?
sections.html:
Hammond has rail service as well as expressways. The South Shore Line stops at Hammond Gateway and South Hammond, and Amtrak's Wolverine serves the Hammond-Whiting station. Chicago Midway is about 25 miles away.

The Borman Expressway and the Indiana Toll Road both run through the area. The city's bus service has changed over the years: NIRBA replaced Hammond Transit in 2010, and EasyGo buses ended on June 30, 2012.

School City of Hammond has two high schools, Hammond Central and Morton, along with 11 elementary schools and two middle schools. A house within reach of a station or an expressway ramp is a selling point worth mentioning to any buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Hammond house if it has flood or sewer damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners sell houses with water damage regularly, but the buyer will want to know the history and the repairs. Hammond had sewer backups in more than 500 homes after the rain of September 17, 2023. A cash buyer can take the house as-is and price the repairs itself.

faqs.q: Do I have to report the sale of a Hammond rental to the city?
faqs.a: Yes. Hammond's rental registration rule says an owner who sells or transfers a rental must notify the Inspections Department within 30 days. Annual registration is due April 15, and the late fee is $500 per unit.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state lists two installments a year, and the 2026 dates were May 11 and November 10. A payment within 30 days after the date carries a 5 percent penalty, and later payment carries 10 percent. Pay your county treasurer.

faqs.q: Where do I get a Hammond building permit?
faqs.a: At the Building Division in Room G1 of City Hall, 5925 Calumet Avenue. The phone is 219-853-6317, and the office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Does Hammond require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: The Hammond pages we read do not list a point-of-sale inspection or certificate of occupancy for a sale. Call the Building Division to confirm for your address, because rules can change.

faqs.q: Who records the deed in Hammond?
faqs.a: The Lake County Recorder records it, after the county auditor has the Indiana sales disclosure form. Your title or escrow company normally handles both.
